name: Geomancer
body:
Geomancer Archetypes

Blood Shaper (Geomancer Archetype)
Protected Geomancer (Geomancer Archetype)
Spirit Speaker (Geomancer Archetype)
Spiritual Healer (Geomancer Archetype)
Steward of Nature (Geomancer Archetype)
Void Cultivator (Geomancer Archetype)

The geomancer is a divine spellcaster that draws power from the spirits inhabiting the world. This class is inspired by several classes from the 3rd edition of the well known tabletop roleplaying games and by Wuxing, Ohaeng, Godai, Shinto, and animism in general.

Role: The role of the geomancer is as wide as a cleric or wizard, though their aptitude depends on what spells they gain from the spirits they commune with.

Alignment: Any. Most geomancers tend toward neutrality, but it is not a hard and fast rule.

Hit Die: d6

Starting Wealth: 3d6 × 10 gp (average 105 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The geomancer’s class skills are: Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (any) (Int), Profession (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier

Class Features

The following are the class features of the geomancer.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Geomancers are proficient with simple weapons. Although the geomancer is not proficient with armor or shields, they do not interfere with their spellcasting.

Spell Casting

A geomancer casts divine spells, which are drawn from a specific set of spells. Their alignment may restrict them from casting certain spells opposed to their moral or ethical beliefs; see Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells of the cleric. A geomancer must choose and prepare their spells in advance, but unlike other prepared casters, they can cast any spell that they have prepared, consuming a spell slot of the appropriate level, assuming they have not used up their spell slots per day for that level.

To prepare or cast a spell, the geomancer must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a geomancer’s spell is 10 + the spell level + their Wisdom modifier.

Like other spellcasters, a geomancer can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day.

Their base daily spell allotment is given on the table below. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Wisdom score (see Table: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells in the Core Rulebook).

A geomancer must spend 1 hour each day communing with the spirits in the world around them to regain their daily allotment of spells. A geomancer may prepare and cast any spell with spirit in the name, specifically affecting spirits, like protection from evil, and summon nature’s ally. Spirits for this purpose are outsiders, fey, and incorporeal undead. The GM may allow certain other thematic spells. Additionally, when communing with the spirits, the geomancer attunes to one of the five elements to grant access to further spells as shown below. To prepare and cast a spell, they must be able to cast spells of that level, but otherwise may prepare any qualifying spell.

Earth– Any spell with earth or stone in the name, or spells that create or affect earth, dirt or stone. Also any spell with the acid, earth, or fear descriptors or spells that provide a Con bonus or Con-based checks.
Fire– Any spell with the fire descriptor, provides a morale bonus, or spells that increase your speeds. Also any spell that provides a bonus to Dex or Dex-based skills.
Metal– Any spell with a metal in the name or spell that directly creates or affects metal. Also any spell with the pain descriptor or spells that cause sadness or despair, or spells that provide a bonus to Str or Str-based skills.
Water– Any spell with the water or healing descriptors, any spell that provides a bonus to Wis or Wis-based skills.
Wood– Any spell with plants or wood in the name or spells that create or affect plants or fungi. Also any spell that provides a competence bonus, or provides a bonus to Cha or Cha-based skills.

To determine the level of the spell slot required for a spell, use the spell-like ability rules. For any spell available only on a 4th or 6th-level caster’s spell list, the spell must have GM approval before being able to be used by the geomancer.

For spell completion or trigger items, you are only considered to possess the requisite spell if it appears on the list of the element you are currently attuned to or the base set of spells for the geomancer.

Like a sorcerer, a geomancer can choose to apply any metamagic feats they know to a prepared spell as they cast it, with the same increase in casting time (see Spontaneous Casting and Metamagic Feats). However, they may also prepare a spell with any metamagic feats they know and cast it without increasing casting time like a wizard. They cannot combine these options—a spell prepared with metamagic feats cannot be further modified with another metamagic feat at the time of casting.

Elemental Speak (Su)

Beginning with 1st level, the geomancer can speak with any fey, outsider, or undead as if they shared a language.

Guardian Spirits (Su)

At 1st level, spirits begin to guide and protect the geomancer. The geomancer gains a +1 bonus on Reflex saves to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to AC against attacks by traps.

Additionally, they gain a +1 bonus on Perception checks to avoid being surprised by a foe. These bonuses increase by 1 every 3 levels thereafter. This ability counts as trap sense for any feat or class prerequisite

Sense Spirits and Elements (Sp)

At 1st level, the geomancer can detect magic spells, magic items, and the presence of certain creatures as a standard action. This functions as detect undead or detect magic except it can only detect the presence of fey, outsiders, or incorporeal undead, and spells or magic items whose construction requirements correspond to the element they attuned to themselves. See the spells ability.

Rebuke Spirits (Su)

At 2nd level, as a standard action, the geomancer can damage spirits in their vicinity. The spirits affected are determined by the element to which you are attuned through your spells ability as follows:

Earth: Any outsider, fey, or incorporeal undead with the water subtype, a swim speed, or the ability to cast a healing spell.
Fire: Any outsider, fey, or incorporeal undead bearing a metal weapon or wearing metal armor or shield, or has an ability or spell with the pain descriptor or causes sadness or despair.
Metal: Any fey creature, or any outsider or incorporeal undead that has spells or abilities that affect plants or fungi.
Water: Any outsider, fey, or incorporeal undead with the fire subtype, or with bardic abilities.
Wood: Any outsider, fey, or incorporeal undead with the earth subtype, or those with spells or abilities with the earth, acid, or fear descriptors.

Any qualifying spirit within 30 feet must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the geomancer’s class level + their Wisdom modifier) or take 1d6 damage. A successful saving throw halves this damage. The damage increases by 1d6 at 4th level and every 2 levels thereafter. This ability is usable a number of times equal to 3 + their Wisdom modifier.

The Selective Channeling feat allows the geomancer to exclude spirits from the effect of this ability.

Girded Against Spirits (Ex)

Beginning with 3rd level, the geomancer is protected against the attacks of spirit creatures. They gain a +2 bonus to saving throws against the abilities or spells of outsiders, fey, or incorporeal undead. This bonus increases by 1 every 4 levels thereafter.

Elemental Mastery (Ex)

At 5th level, you have dedicated yourself to a master of the magics of one of the five elements. Choose one of the five elements:

Earth, Fire, Metal, Water, or Wood. Once the choice has been made, it can’t be changed later. When casting spells prepared from that element, assuming you have communed with it, you increase your caster level by 1.

At 11th, and 17th levels, you gain an additional choice to either increase the caster level of the same element, or increase the caster level of another element.

Spiritual Guidance (Su)

At 5th level, the spirits can help break the geomancer’s mind free from mental effects. If the geomancer fails a saving throw and is continuing to be affected by an enchantment spell, they may make an additional saving throw the following round at the beginning of their turn to break the effect. The geomancer only gains one extra chance against an effect.

Spiritual Boon (Su)

At 6th level, the geomancer gains some assistance from the spirits in the world around them.

They choose one spiritual boon from the list below. The geomancer gains another spiritual boon at 12th and 18th levels. You can only gain a boon once.

Ape or chimpanzee: You gain a +2 bonus on Perform checks with a Perform skill of your choice and you gain the chosen Perform skill as a class skill.
Badger or boar: You gain a +2 bonus on Intimidate checks and gain Intimidate as a class skill.
Bear or boar: You gain Toughness as a bonus feat.
Butterfly: Once per day, as a free action, you may change one of your daily prepared geomancer spells of 0th-level or 1st-level for another spell of equal level belonging to the attuned element you selected when you prepared your daily geomancer spells.
Cicada: You gain a +1 bonus to natural armor and a +2 bonus on Constitution-based checks.
Cockroach or tardigrade: You gain a +2 bonus on Survival checks and gain Survival as a class skill.
Crane: You gain a +2 bonus on Heal and Disguise checks and one of these skills as a class skill.
Dog: You gain a +2 bonus on Handle Animal checks and gain Handle Animal as a class skill.
Dolphin or shark: You gain a +2 bonus on Swim checks and gain Swim as a class skill.
Dragonfly: You gain a +2 bonus to initiative checks.
Eagle, hawk, or owl: You gain a +2 bonus on Perception checks and gain Perception as a class skill.
Fire: You gain a +2 bonus to Acrobatics checks and gain Acrobatics as a class skill.
Fox or coyote: You gain a +2 bonus to Bluff and Disguise checks and gain one of these skills as a class skill.
Monkey: You gain a +2 bonus on Climb checks and gain Climb as a class skill.
Panther or tiger: You gain a +2 bonus on Stealth checks and gain Stealth as a class skill.
Peacock: You gain a +2 bonus to Perform and Intimidate checks and gain one of these skills as a class skill.
Octopus or squid: You gain a +2 bonus on Escape Artist checks and gain Escape Artist as a class skill.
Spider: You gain a +2 bonus on Climb checks and gain Climb as a class skill.
Stone: You gain a +2 bonus on Fortitude saves.
Toad, turtle, or snake: You gain a +2 bonus on Sense Motive checks and gain Sense Motive as a class skill.
Water: You gain a +2 bonus on Will saves.
Wind: You gain a +2 bonus on Reflex saves.
Wolf: You gain low-light vision.
Spiritual Assistance (Su)

At 9th level, the geomancer can delegate the concentration of a spell onto the spirits that aid them as a swift action. The geomancer can act normally while their spirits concentrate on the spell.

The spirits can concentrate on only one spell at a time.

If necessary to maintain the spell, the spirits make concentration checks for the geomancer, using the geomancer’s normal concentration modifier. The spirits do not have to make concentration checks for circumstances such as the geomancer taking damage.

The spirits themselves are not present for anyone to interrupt or otherwise interact with.

Exorcism (Su)

At 13th level, as a full round action, the geomancer can attempt to end a possession effect and expel the possessing creature with a successful melee touch attack. To do so, the geomancer must make a caster level check against the DC of the possession effect, or if there is no DC, then 10 + the HD of the possessing creature + their Charisma modifier. If the caster level check succeeds, the possessing creature is expelled and unable to possess the same creature for 24 hours. Also, if you choose, you can expend a use of your rebuke spirits ability to deal your rebuke spirits’ damage (no save) to the expelled possessing creature whenever you successfully expel them with your exorcism ability.

Spiritual Master (Ex)

At 20th level, the geomancer becomes a master of the spiritual world. When attuning to an element when preparing spells, they can attune to two elements. However, the elements must be complimentary as follows:

Earth must be paired with fire or metal.
Fire must be paired with wood or earth.
Metal must be paired with earth or water.
Water must be paired with metal or wood.
Wood must be paired with fire or water.

Additionally, the geomancer can become like a spirit themself. They are able to cast ethereal jaunt once per day using their class level as the caster level.
